question.problem: What is the limit of the sequence ${a}_{n}=\frac{({n}^{3}-1)({n}^{3}+1)}{{n}^{4}({n}^{2}-2)}$ for $n\ge 1?$
question.worked_solution:
First, we multiply out the numerator and denominator of the sequence and get

$$
{a}_{n}=\frac{({n}^{3}-1)({n}^{3}+1)}{{n}^{4}({n}^{2}-2)}=\frac{{n}^{6}-1}{{n}^{6}-2{n}^{4}}.
$$

So to find the limit, we will need to compute

$$
{lim}_{n\to \infty }⁡{a}_{n}={lim}_{n\to \infty }⁡\frac{{n}^{6}-1}{{n}^{6}-2{n}^{4}}.
$$

The dominant term in the denominator is ${n}^{6},$ so we divide the numerator and the denominator by ${n}^{6}$ and get

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{n\to \infty }⁡\frac{{n}^{6}-1}{{n}^{6}-2{n}^{4}} & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }⁡\frac{(\frac{{n}^{6}}{{n}^{6}}-\frac{1}{{n}^{6}})}{(\frac{{n}^{6}}{{n}^{6}}-\frac{2{n}^{4}}{{n}^{6}})} \\  & ={lim}_{n\to \infty }⁡\frac{(1-\frac{1}{{n}^{6}})}{(1-\frac{2}{{n}^{2}})} \\  & =\frac{1-0}{1-0} \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Consequently, the sequence converges and its limit is $1.$
